notes: Run these cases in both Claude Code and Codex. Slash skill names are shorthand: invoke /feature-spec:feature-spec or /feature-spec:feature-spec-plan in Claude Code, and $feature-spec or $feature-spec-plan in Codex. Use the current host question and subagent tools; record its version and any degraded coverage.
Lives inside the skill folder because that is where skill-creator looks for it. It is not part of the canonical SKILL.md / scripts / references / assets layout and is never loaded at runtime.

No fixture files ship with this suite, deliberately. A spec plugin is judged on how it interviews about a REAL codebase, and four invented sample projects would only prove it can interview about four invented sample projects. Each case states the repo it needs; the operator points it at a real one.

Where a case needs a feature-spec artifact rather than a codebase, `scripts/test-checks.sh` already builds one from the shipped skeleton in `references/tree-format.md` — so the fixture cannot drift from the documented format. Generate rather than store.
Cases 1 and 2 are refusals: the skill passes by NOT producing a spec. First on purpose — a tool that cannot decline is a tool that always bills.

Cases 3 and 10 are the input-driven path: a complete brief must produce no clarifying round at all, and a brief with one false claim must produce exactly the question that claim deserves. They are what tells a run that reads its input from one that interviews regardless.
The token and duration figures the harness records are the point of this file: the plugin itself reports no token figure, so this is where one comes from.

Cases 7-9 cover /feature-spec-plan. Case 8 is the one that matters: the backwards coverage check — that no requirement was silently dropped — is the plugin's central claim about the plan stage, and it is the failure a plan that reads complete will pass every eyeball test on.
Case 9 is the second-visit path. A plan is written once and amended repeatedly, and `extend` preserving the statuses of work already done is the property a single manual try never exercises.

evals.expected_output: A refusal. The idea is too vague to slug, so the skill asks one clarifying question, says an unformed idea needs an interview before a spec, names /grill-me for that, and stops without creating a directory or writing any file.
assertions: No directory was created under docs/specs/
No tree.md, spec.md or GLOSSARY.md was written anywhere
The response asks at most one clarifying question
The response names /grill-me as the place to start, as a suggestion and not a call
The response does not render a question-tool picker of clarifying questions
The response does not begin a numbered round

evals.prompt: /feature-spec change the submit button label from 'Send' to 'Submit'
evals.expected_output: A refusal on the grounds that there is nothing here a spec would decide. The user is left a way to go on if they disagree.
assertions: No directory was created under docs/specs/
The response states that this does not need a spec, or that there is no decision in it
The response says the run goes on if the user disagrees
No clarifying round was rendered

evals.prompt: /feature-spec <path to a brief that settles every coverage category, such as one written by /grill-me>
evals.repo: the real repo the brief is about, so its claims can be checked against code
evals.expected_output: No clarifying round. The run says so and why, builds the record from the brief with (r0) entries, checks the brief's claims against the code, then drafts, runs the critic and writes the spec.
assertions: No picker or numbered block of clarifying questions was rendered (a strategy picker is allowed)
The response says that no clarifying round was needed and gives the reason
tree.md's Protocol block reads Round: 0 of 2
Every Settled entry is tagged (r0) and names the brief, or the request, in its Why
Nothing the brief lists as an assumption or an open question appears under ## Settled
Each claim the brief makes about the repo has a Grounding facts entry with a verdict
check-tree.sh exits 0 on the resulting tree.md
check-spec.sh --tree <tree.md> exits 0 on the resulting spec.md
critique.md names a verdict of ship or fix-first with a calibrated confidence
spec.draft.md does not exist after the run
The final report states clarifying rounds and critic passes as counts
The final report states no token count, context percentage or elapsed cost

evals.prompt: /feature-spec <a real feature you would actually want spec'd>
evals.repo: a real Swift, TypeScript or Python repo — whichever stack layer you want to exercise. A monorepo is the more interesting test: the stack must be detected from the FEATURE'S scope, not the repo's overall shape.
evals.expected_output: A run from a bare idea: the right stack layer loaded before fact-finders are dispatched, at most two clarifying rounds, a coverage table after each, a critic pass, and a spec whose tags all resolve.
assertions: The stack layer loaded matches the feature's scope, not merely the repo's most common language
That layer's two references were loaded before any fact-finder was dispatched
Independent fact-finders were dispatched concurrently within the host worker limit, with excess work queued
No more than 5 questions were asked in any one round
No more than 2 rounds ran
A coverage table with all ten taxonomy category names verbatim was printed after every round
Any Clear* entry is written as 'Clear* (n deferred)' with its count
At least one question was collapsed by a grounding fact rather than asked
Whatever was still open after the last round appears in the spec as [NEEDS CLARIFICATION]
check-tree.sh and check-spec.sh both exit 0 on the final artifacts
critique.md names a verdict of ship or fix-first with a calibrated confidence

evals.prompt: /feature-spec <slug of a run whose design record is corrupted> --resume
evals.repo: any. Take a valid tree.md from an unfinished run, delete its ## Sessions section and rename one coverage category.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports which section failed and offers the doctor's repair, rather than drafting from a half-understood record.
assertions: No spec.md was written
The response names the specific section that failed to parse
The response either ran check-tree.sh --doctor or reproduced its repair output
The response offers a route forward — repair or archive-and-restart
The response does not guess at the missing content

evals.prompt: /feature-spec <slug of a spec written by case 3 or 4> — <a changed decision>
evals.repo: the same repo as the run that produced the spec
evals.expected_output: An amendment. The existing spec is offered amend/restart/read-only rather than overwritten; the superseded answer is struck through, not deleted; and no identifier is renumbered.
assertions: The user was offered amend, restart and read-only before anything was written
The previous tree.md content is still present — the superseded answer appears struck through, not removed
A new session line was appended to ## Sessions rather than the section being rewritten
check-spec.sh was run with --prev pointing at the previous spec.md
No FR or SC identifier changed its meaning between the old and new spec
Any withdrawn requirement remains in place marked (withdrawn) rather than being deleted
The spec directory was not re-dated

evals.prompt: /feature-spec-plan <slug of a spec whose requirements are all deferred, i.e. every FR carries a [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker>
evals.repo: any, with a feature-spec spec directory
evals.expected_output: A plan is still written, every task Blocked, and the report leads with the markers to resolve first. It does not silently pick an answer for any marker, and it does not refuse.
assertions: plan/plan.md and at least one plan/tasks/T0N.md were written
Every task file carries Status: Blocked and a Blocked by: line
Every [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker in spec.md appears in plan.md's ## Open questions carried from the spec
No action item resolves a marker by choosing one branch of it
The report names the markers to resolve before work starts

evals.prompt: /feature-spec-plan <slug of the spec written by case 3 or 4>
evals.repo: the same repo that spec was written against
evals.expected_output: A plan whose tasks cover every FR and SC in the spec, with done-conditions quoted from the spec rather than restated, and every implementation choice recorded as an assumption with its reversal cost.
assertions: Every FR and SC identifier in spec.md is either named in some task's Covers: line or listed under ## Not planned with a reason
No task's Covers: line names an identifier the spec does not define
Every line under a task's ## Done when appears verbatim in spec.md
plan.md's ## Task graph table agrees with the Status, Covers and Depends on of every task file
## Plan assumptions is non-empty, and every entry states a reversal cost
The first milestone contains only tasks covering P1 requirements
No task file states an estimate in hours, days or story points
check-plan.sh exits 0 against the written plan

evals.prompt: /feature-spec-plan <the same slug as case 8, after amending the spec to add one requirement, and after marking T01 Done by hand>, then the same command again with --extend
evals.expected_output: The first run prints the plan's state, names the three choices — extend, replan, read-only — and writes nothing. With --extend, T01 keeps its Done status and a new task covers the added requirement.
assertions: Without a flag, the response names extend, replan and read-only, says how each is taken, and writes nothing
With --extend, T01 still reads Status: Done
With --extend, no existing task id was renumbered or reused
With --extend, the added requirement is covered by a task that did not exist before
plan.md's task graph was regenerated rather than hand-edited

evals.prompt: /feature-spec <path to a brief that is complete except for one claim about the repo that is false>
evals.repo: the real repo the brief is about
evals.expected_output: The false claim is reported as contradicted, with where the code says otherwise, and becomes the one thing asked about or a correction to the problem statement. Nothing the brief decided is asked again.
assertions: The grounding summary names the claim as contradicted and cites path:line
The Grounding facts entry for that claim carries the verdict contradicted
At most one clarifying round ran
No question asked the user something the brief had already decided
The spec does not assert the false claim
check-tree.sh and check-spec.sh both exit 0 on the final artifacts
